x: Stirling Wakeley to win a 24 Hour Track Walk at Motspur Park in 1948 and helping fellow Belgravians, Gordon Doubleday and Syd. Spencer compete successfully in races at 100 miles and over.

Another AGM visitor was SYD SPENCER former 'B' Division Police and Belgrave walker - now on the Judges list. It was a great pleasure when our Vice-President from Delhi, RANJIT BHATIA paid us a visit in late September and competed in our road race.
In 1952 another classic route was walked, Bath to London (Chiswick) and Chelsea policeman Syd Spencer recorded a very fine 20:09:45 for badge No. 181.
Gordon Doubleday, F.Herring, Sid Spencer and Bill Urry followed at an easier pace. Jack Bidgood eventually went away from the others and at Chequers Horley was in 9th position.

Bill Ashford, still working in Holland, made one of his week-end trips coincide with the function. Syd Spencer is often seen judging walking events. When he was a policeman at Chelsea he gained us many new members.
He looked very fit and after asking after old friends was off round the course with SYD SPENCER - did they sign on any new members as they used to in the old days?

Chief Judge was our own GEORGE BENTLEY and amongst those judging were FRED DENNY - happily recovered from his operation, FRANK JARVIS who has also had a bout in hospital, evergreen HAROLD KING with SYD SPENCER, HARRY SHIELDS and BILL TRUE to cast their eagle eyes on the proceedings.

The judges panel was headed by Syd Spencer, who did the job with his usual quiet efficiency. Also judging were evergreen Harold King, Bill True and Joe Wilson, and in the grade III category, Barbara Dunsford.

Amongst the Judges were Joe Coleman, Fred Denny, Barbara Dunsford, Harold King, Syd Spencer, Bill True and Joe Wilson. Ray Hall together with Fred and Bill were logging them in, the sheets going in to Jack Goswell and Frank Jarvis, assisted by their wives to get out the results.

Referee for the race was past President Ray Hall, whilst Chief Judge was Syd Spencer, also judging were Joe Coleman, Fred Denny, Barbara Dunsford, Harold King, Bill True and Joe Wilson, recording was Frank Webb and of course masterminding the final result in the back room was Jack Goswell ably assisted by Joan.
We are all sorry to learn that Syd Spencer, former Police Long Distance walker and nowadays a Walking Judge has been in hospital with leg trouble.

Amongst the judges were George Bentley, Fred Denny, Barbara Dunsford, Sid Spencer, Bill True and Joe Wilson and refereeing was Ray Hall. Again the course was changed using three laps of the hills using a less steep hill than previous.
We regret to learn that on Sunday, 17th January 1982 Syd Spencer passed away. 'Syd Spencer' was 76 years old and had been a member for many years.
On the officials side we have lost over the last few months Harry Shields and Syd Spencer, and although not a member of the club, Tom Reynolds.
